messages.task:
You are a financial analysis assistant.  You have access to several specialised data-retrieval tools (documented below) that connect to an internal finance database.  Use them, together with logical reasoning, to answer the end-user’s question.

SCENARIO
A large technology reseller monitors its working-capital efficiency through metrics such as Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO) and Days Purchases Outstanding (DPO).  The firm also discloses trends in capital expenditures (CAPEX) for several recent years.  Management notes that CAPEX rose in 2017 as the company upgraded information-technology systems, while in the prior year it fell following completion of a major office build-out in 2015.  Exact figures for CAPEX are stored in the internal database that your tools can query.

TOOLS AT YOUR DISPOSAL
• list_expense_categories() → list[str]
  Return all available expense category names.

• get_category_id(category_name: str) → int
  Map a human-readable category name to its internal identifier.

• list_years_with_quarterly_data() → list[int]
  List years for which any quarterly expense information exists.

• get_quarterly_expenses(year: int, category_name: str) → list[tuple[int,int]]
  Retrieve (quarter, amount_in_millions) pairs for a specified year & category.

• get_annual_expense(year: int, category_name: str) → int
  Convenience helper that returns the sum of the four quarterly figures for the given year & category.

• compute_simple_average(numbers: list[int]) → int
  Compute the integer (floor) average of a list of numbers.

Supplementary / potentially irrelevant tools
• get_total_expenses_for_year(year: int) → int
• get_random_financial_fact() → str

YOUR TASK
Use any combination of the tools above to answer the following question and output only the final numeric answer (no additional text):

Question: What was the average capital expenditures, in millions, for 2016 and 2015?

Think step-by-step, call tools when needed, and provide the single integer result.
